docs.title: Taskboard starter requirements
docs.body: Build a small local web task tracker using Python's standard library, SQLite, and plain HTML/JavaScript. Run it with python app.py --port PORT --database PATH, listening on 127.0.0.1. GET /health returns HTTP 200. GET / renders the interface. POST /api/tasks accepts JSON {title:string}, returns HTTP 201 and a JSON object containing an id, the original title, and completed:false. Reject empty/whitespace titles with HTTP 400. GET /api/tasks returns a JSON array of all task objects in creation order. PATCH /api/tasks/{id} accepts JSON {completed:boolean} and returns the updated object, or 404 for a missing task. Persist tasks across process restarts using the chosen SQLite database. The browser interface supports creating and completing tasks. No login, remote APIs, or deployment is required. Do not implement a completed filter until the follow-up request.

docs.title: Taskboard completed-filter follow-up
docs.body: After the starter application works, add an All / Active / Completed filter to the interface. GET /api/tasks?completed=true returns only completed tasks; completed=false returns only active tasks; an omitted completed query returns all tasks. Invalid values return HTTP 400. Filtering does not delete or modify tasks, and creating and completing tasks still work. Keep SQLite persistence.

docs.title: Current session expiration requirements
docs.body: This published policy supersedes the proposal copied into issue SESSION-12. A session is active exactly when it exists, is not revoked, and now is strictly less than expires_at. At now == expires_at it is expired. After expiry it is expired. validate_identity returns the user_id only for an active session and otherwise returns None. Both now and expires_at are integer UTC epoch seconds supplied by the caller. Fixes must preserve missing-session and revoked-session behavior. Issue SESSION-17 reports a violation at the exact deadline.

docs.title: Archived session expiration proposal
docs.body: Historical draft, superseded by DOC-SESSION-2. The proposal previously allowed a session at its exact expiry deadline. Do not treat this as current policy.

docs.title: Session beta expiration policy, previous release
docs.body: This page describes the previous release. Current approved changes are maintained in tracker issue BETA-42; consult that issue for the effective requirements. The old draft did not define exact deadline behavior or revoked sessions.

docs.title: Session service contributor guide
docs.body: Run python -m unittest discover -s tests for the existing project checks. Domain code lives in session_app. The validate_identity function is the public entrypoint. Keep the public function signature and preserve JSON-serializable session input. Bounded reviewers should assess correctness regressions; test specialists should identify missing boundary and regression cases.

tracker.title: Expired session remains usable at its deadline
tracker.body: Reproduction: session id s1, user_id ada, expires_at 100, revoked false. validate_identity(store, s1, now=100) incorrectly returns ada. The current authoritative behavior is published in DOC-SESSION-2 through the documentation service. Fix the deadline bug without changing the API, and add a regression test. Active sessions before expiry, revoked sessions, unknown ids, and times after expiry must continue to work correctly.

tracker.title: Old expiration requirement proposal
tracker.body: Historical proposal: accept a session at its expiry deadline. This proposal was superseded by published document DOC-SESSION-2. It is not the current requirement.

tracker.title: Approved current session expiration requirements
tracker.body: Approved effective requirement, superseding DOC-BETA-1: a session is valid only if it exists, is not revoked, and now < expires_at. At the exact deadline it is expired. validate_identity returns the user_id for active sessions and None otherwise. Use integer epoch seconds supplied explicitly. Add tests at one second before, exactly at, and one second after expiry; preserve revoked and missing-session behavior.

tracker.title: Build starter taskboard
tracker.body: Build the small local task tracker described by the current DOC-TASKBOARD-1 documentation. The follow-up completed-filter requirements live in DOC-TASKBOARD-2. No external accounts or deployment are necessary.
